# `write-clear`

Flags comment sentences that are hard to read, using
[retext-readability](https://github.com/retextjs/retext-readability).

The rule scores each sentence with seven readability formulas. When enough of them agree that a
sentence is too dense for the target reading age, it reports the sentence. Dense, jargon-packed
prose — the house style of a rushed AI comment — is what this catches.

It reuses the same logical comments as the other rules and points at the sentence in the source.
It provides no autofix: clearer wording is a writing decision, not a mechanical one.

## Options

A single options object tunes the target reading level.

```js
'comment-slop/write-clear': ['warn', { age: 22 }]
```

| Option      | Type     | Default | Description                                                  |
| :---------- | :------- | :------ | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `age`       | `number` | `18`    | Target reading age. Raise it to tolerate denser prose.       |
| `minWords`  | `number` | `5`     | Skip sentences shorter than this.                            |
| `threshold` | `number` | `4/7`   | Share of the seven formulas that must agree before flagging. |

## Examples

### Dense prose

Dense, jargon-packed sentences — the house style of a rushed AI comment — score as hard to read across the seven formulas. The rule points at the offending sentence.

The following patterns are considered problems:

```js
// The utilization of a load-bearing abstraction facilitates comprehensive orchestration of downstream dependency resolution.
// "comment-slop/write-clear": ["error"]
// Message: Hard to read for a target age of 18 — simplify the sentence.
```

The following patterns are not considered problems:

```js
// Reuses the cached result instead of recomputing it.
// "comment-slop/write-clear": ["error"]
```

### Short sentences

Short notes are left alone: by default the rule skips sentences under five words, so a terse comment with one long word does not trip it. Lower `minWords` to check them too.

The following patterns are considered problems:

```js
// Instantiate the orchestrator.
// "comment-slop/write-clear": ["error",{"minWords":1}]
// Message: Hard to read for a target age of 18 — simplify the sentence.
```

The following patterns are not considered problems:

```js
// Instantiate the orchestrator.
// "comment-slop/write-clear": ["error"]
```

### Configurable reading level

Raise `age` to allow denser prose. A sentence flagged at the default reading age passes at a higher one.

The following patterns are considered problems:

```js
// Subsequent invocations reuse the memoized computation rather than recomputing the derived aggregate.
// "comment-slop/write-clear": ["error"]
// Message: Hard to read for a target age of 18 — simplify the sentence.
```

The following patterns are not considered problems:

```js
// Subsequent invocations reuse the memoized computation rather than recomputing the derived aggregate.
// "comment-slop/write-clear": ["error",{"age":30}]
```
